title: Strings and entropy

milestone.title: Ground Rules, Tools and the PE Format

description:
Two triage tools from lesson 1.05:

```cpp
struct FoundString { std::size_t offset; std::string text; bool wide; };

std::vector<FoundString> findStrings(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes, std::size_t minLength);
double entropy(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes, std::size_t begin, std::size_t size);
```

**findStrings** finds text of at least `minLength` characters, where a character is a printable byte from 0x20 to 0x7E:
- **ASCII** strings: runs of printable bytes.
- **Wide** (UTF-16LE) strings: runs of pairs "printable byte, then 0x00", starting at any offset. `text` holds just the characters (`"Wide"`, not the zeros), and `wide` is true.
- Results are sorted by offset; at the same offset an ASCII string comes first. Report each whole run once, not the shorter runs inside it.

**entropy** is the Shannon entropy in bits per byte of `size` bytes starting at `begin`: `-sum(p * log2(p))` over the byte values present, where `p` is that value's count divided by `size`. An empty range has entropy 0.
hints: Do the two kinds in two separate passes over the bytes, then sort the results by offset. In the wide pass, move two bytes at a time while you are inside a run.
For entropy, count each byte value in a `std::array<std::size_t, 256>`, then add up `-p * log2(p)` for the values whose count is not zero.
lessonTitle: Triage - First Impressions of a Binary
